title: FinanceQuest
summary: A 24-month financial life simulation built for the NTU Tech For Good 2026 Hackathon, combining interactive decision-making, AI guidance and machine-learning goal predictions.
long: FinanceQuest teaches personal finance through a simulated two-year journey. Players make three decisions each month, respond to changing life events and balance financial goals with happiness and stress.
problem: Personal finance concepts can feel abstract when they are taught only through static examples. FinanceQuest turns those concepts into a hands-on experience where players can see how decisions compound over time.
approach: Built a Python and Pygame simulation with character setup, monthly decisions and dynamic life events.
Integrated Finley, a conversational financial assistant built with LangChain and Azure OpenAI, for on-demand guidance.
Used gameplay data from the first six months with a scikit-learn model to estimate the likelihood of achieving a selected goal.
Created post-game analytics with pandas and Matplotlib to show net-worth progression and asset composition.
results: Top 10 finalist at NTU Tech For Good 2026
AI assistant and ML-based goal predictions

title: SG Enable Support & Management Portal
summary: A Flask application bringing participant services and social-service operations into one central platform.
long: The system provides two connected experiences: a Participant Portal for discovering activities and requesting support, and a Staff Portal for managing operational records and monitoring activity.
problem: Participants and caregivers need accessible activity discovery and support channels, while staff need centralised tools to manage registrations, enquiries, activity records and operational information.
approach: Designed separate participant and staff experiences with distinct workflows.
Implemented activity discovery, registration and enquiry submission for participants.
Built staff tools for enquiry tracking, activity moderation, financial multi-payment support and operational dashboards.
Used WTForms validation, Python Shelve persistence and Chart.js visualisations.

title: Text & Social Analytics
summary: An NLP pipeline analysing 5,000+ e-commerce reviews across Owala, Stanley, YETI and Hydro Flask to surface customer sentiment and recurring complaints.
long: The project combines dynamic review collection, text preprocessing and sentiment classification to turn unstructured customer feedback into product insights.
problem: Large volumes of online reviews make it difficult to manually identify recurring product issues and understand how customer sentiment differs across brands.
approach: Collected reviews from dynamically loaded e-commerce pages using SeleniumBase.
Cleaned and transformed raw review text for downstream analysis.
Developed a sentiment classifier to categorise reviews as positive or negative.
Reviewed recurring complaints and translated patterns into potential product-quality recommendations.
results: 60% recall for negative reviews; class imbalance remains an important limitation

title: Topic Modelling
summary: An end-to-end NLP pipeline using Latent Dirichlet Allocation to uncover themes in World Bank project documents.
long: The project explores how topic modelling can organise large collections of unstructured reports into interpretable thematic groups, reducing reliance on manual document review.
problem: World Bank reports contain large volumes of unstructured text. Reviewing every document manually makes it difficult to classify the corpus consistently and discover recurring themes at scale.
approach: Prepared English-language documents and removed HTML, non-alphabetic characters, Unicode noise and stopwords.
Applied NLTK and spaCy for tokenisation and lemmatisation.
Implemented LDA with Gensim to discover latent topics.
Compared topic configurations using coherence and perplexity, with Alpha and Eta tuning where applicable.
Used PyLDAvis to inspect topic prevalence, inter-topic distances and salient terms.
results: Automated thematic grouping of unstructured reports
Topics explored included urban development, financial infrastructure and environmental policy
Human interpretation is still required to label topics

title: Diabetes Prediction
summary: A clinical-risk prediction project using Scikit-learn, with model evaluation focused on identifying positive cases.
long: This project explores machine-learning classification for diabetes risk screening and considers why recall matters when a missed positive prediction can have meaningful consequences.
problem: A predictive model for health screening should be evaluated beyond overall accuracy. In particular, the ability to identify actual positive cases is important when false negatives carry a cost.
approach: Explored and prepared a structured dataset for modelling.
Applied SMOTE to address class imbalance in the training data.
Trained and compared classification models using Scikit-learn.
Evaluated model performance with a focus on recall and the trade-offs between model outcomes.
results: Approximately 65% recall reported on the portfolio project card
Evaluation emphasised reducing missed positive cases
A model output is not a medical diagnosis

title: Green Plan 2030
summary: A Power BI dashboard exploring Singapore's sustainability progress using plastic-waste datasets and visual analysis.
long: The dashboard brings together Singapore and global plastic-waste data to examine waste generation, disposal and recycling patterns, with forecasting used to explore possible trends.
problem: Sustainability data can be difficult to interpret when indicators are spread across different datasets. A consolidated dashboard makes trends easier to explore.
approach: Combined and transformed datasets using Power Query.
Built Power BI visuals to explore waste generation, disposal and recycling.
Used linear regression forecasts to examine possible future trends.
results: Forecasting included as an exploratory component

title: Protein Tracker
summary: A Power BI dashboard tracking daily protein intake against a 90g target, with meal-level and time-based views.
long: The dashboard turns daily nutrition logs into a view of protein intake, consistency and potential gaps across meals and training phases.
problem: Tracking intake over time can make it easier to understand whether daily nutrition habits are consistent and where improvements may be needed.
approach: Structured meal-level protein intake data for analysis.
Built daily, weekly and monthly dashboard views.
Compared intake against a 90g daily goal and highlighted meal-level contributions.
Included consistency metrics and automated insights.

title: InvestED App
summary: A beginner-friendly Flask web application teaching investment concepts through interactive compound-interest projections.
long: InvestED provides accessible financial-planning tools that let users explore how savings, returns and time can affect long-term goals.
problem: Investment concepts can be intimidating for beginners. Interactive scenarios help make the relationship between contributions, time and potential returns easier to understand.
approach: Built a Flask web application for financial-literacy scenarios.
Added compound-interest projections and investment comparisons.
Included financial-freedom calculations and interactive Chart.js visualisations.

title: HDB Resale Price Dashboard
summary: A D3.js dashboard exploring Singapore HDB resale prices, property trends and nearby amenities through linked charts and geospatial views.
long: The dashboard combines multiple datasets into an interactive exploration of resale-price patterns and location context.
problem: Property prices are influenced by multiple factors, and static charts can make it difficult to explore relationships across time, location and nearby amenities.
approach: Integrated six datasets into a unified visualisation experience.
Built linked charts and dynamic filters with D3.js.
Added geospatial mapping and amenity-proximity context.
Presented KPI summaries to support exploration of resale-price trends.

title: Waste Image & News Article Classification
eyebrow: Applied deep learning · Computer vision & NLP
summary: A deep-learning assignment comparing computer-vision models for waste images and NLP models for news-article classification.
long: The project explores two different machine-learning tasks: classifying waste images and categorising news articles. It compares model approaches and evaluates performance using appropriate classification metrics.
problem: Image and text classification involve different data representations and modelling choices. The project compares approaches across both domains and evaluates their strengths and limitations.
approach: Prepared and processed image and text datasets for modelling.
Compared Custom CNN, Improved CNN and fine-tuned VGG16 for waste-image classification.
Explored BiLSTM and DistilBERT for news-article classification.
Compared model performance using test accuracy and classification metrics.
results: VGG16 achieved 81.49% test accuracy on waste images
DistilBERT achieved 94.24% test accuracy on news classification
Compared computer-vision and NLP model approaches

title: Employee Burnout Prediction & MLOps Portal
summary: A team MLOps project integrating an employee-burnout prediction model with data versioning, automated testing and a Flask application.
long: This project brings together a predictive modelling workflow and application delivery practices, showing how a model can be managed as part of a broader machine-learning system.
problem: A machine-learning model is only one part of a usable solution. Data, model versions, testing and application integration also need to be managed.
approach: Developed an employee-burnout prediction model as part of a team project.
Integrated machine-learning workflow components and data versioning.
Included automated testing and a Flask application.
results: Model workflow integrated with a Flask application
Data versioning and automated testing included
status: Project overview — detail page to be added

title: AI Budgeting & Financial Literacy Coach
summary: A financial-literacy coaching prototype using Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite fine-tuning on Google Vertex AI, with evaluation and a retrieval-augmented generation extension.
long: A simulated retail-banking use case exploring how a fine-tuned language model can provide structured, persona-driven financial coaching. The work includes a supervised fine-tuning workflow, controlled training experiments, a side-by-side evaluation interface and a RAG extension.
problem: General-purpose language models may not consistently follow a specialised financial-coach persona or produce the structured responses expected in a banking scenario. The project explores fine-tuning and retrieval as complementary ways to shape and ground responses.
approach: Fine-tuned Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite on Google Vertex AI using a 10-example JSONL dataset for a simulated DBS retail-banking use case.
Created a JSONL training pipeline and automated Google Cloud Storage bucket creation and data upload.
Compared training configurations of 3, 5 and 7 epochs by analysing accuracy and loss curves; the CV describes epoch 4 as the selected balance.
Built a Gradio interface to compare base and fine-tuned model outputs across seen, unseen and out-of-scope test cases.
Designed a RAG extension using Vertex AI Embeddings (text-embedding-004) and ChromaDB.
results: Compared model outputs across seen, unseen and out-of-scope prompts
RAG extension demonstrated as a complementary grounding approach

title: Singapore Water Quality Data Pipeline
summary: A Snowflake Medallion Architecture pipeline processing PUB drinking-water quality data and a Kaggle potability dataset into analytics-ready layers.
long: The project designs a Bronze–Silver–Gold data architecture in Snowflake to ingest, clean and curate PUB drinking-water quality data from 2019–2022 alongside a 3,276-record Kaggle potability dataset. A Streamlit data product connects to Snowflake for exploration and model reporting.
problem: Raw water-quality datasets contain missing values and inconsistent string representations. Downstream analytics needs a reliable, curated layer rather than repeating cleaning and transformation in the presentation layer.
approach: Designed Bronze, Silver and Gold layers in Snowflake to ingest, cleanse and curate PUB drinking-water quality data and a 3,276-record Kaggle potability dataset.
Wrote SQL transformations using COALESCE for missing-value imputation and CASE / TRY_TO_DOUBLE to parse inconsistent raw strings into numeric values.
Built Gold-layer materialized views to pre-aggregate analytics-ready tables and reduce frontend processing.
Developed a Streamlit data product with live Snowflake connectivity, exploratory visualisations and a Random Forest model.
Reported model accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and feature importance.
results: Streamlit data product with live Snowflake connectivity
Random Forest evaluation and feature-importance reporting
